paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: a faith that leans on one person is a faith that can fall when that person is gone. Joash did right while Jehoiada was alive, but the minute Jehoiada was gone, Joash listened to the officials and they walked away from the house of the LORD (2 Chronicles 24:17-18). I can't say why he turned, but I think his faith never got its own roots. Baker, ask yourself whose voice your faith is leaning on, and then get your own roots down in the Word.

And look how patient God is. He sent prophets to bring the people back, and when they would not listen, He sent Zechariah with a plain word: "Because you have forsaken the LORD, He has forsaken you." (2 Chronicles 24:19-20). The warning was a door left open, and the people shut it. Joash even forgot the kindness Jehoiada had shown him and killed Jehoiada's son (2 Chronicles 24:22), so I think this one is heavy.

The ending shows that the LORD takes what is done to His servants seriously. A few Aramean men beat a very great army, because Judah had forsaken the LORD (2 Chronicles 24:24). Joash was not buried in the tombs of the kings (2 Chronicles 24:25). So listen to God's voice while it's still a warning, baker, and stay close to Him whether or not anyone around you does. The story isn't over, because the next king, Amaziah, is just stepping in.
